name: The Asterran Realm
summary: A feudal patchwork of river valleys ruled by Lord Brannoc under a distant king. Peasants farm and mill, guilds control trade, and the Chapel of the Twin Lights interprets the will of the moons. Medicine is mostly prayer and herb-lore, which makes the new sickness terrifying.

government.ruler: Lord Aldric Brannoc, vassal of King Oswin III
government.description: Land is held in oath from the lord; reeves govern villages; justice is the lord's court.

beliefs: The Twin Lights watch every deed; a sin done under both moons is doubly cursed.
Sickness is punishment for hidden sin, cleansed by confession and offerings.
Forest spirits take those who wander Thornwood after dark.

socialClasses.name: Nobility
socialClasses.description: The lord's family and knights; own the land.

socialClasses.name: Clergy
socialClasses.description: Priests and acolytes of the Twin Lights.

socialClasses.name: Guildfolk
socialClasses.description: Millers, smiths, weavers and merchants of the towns.

socialClasses.name: Serfs
socialClasses.description: Peasants bound to the lord's land.

laws: Poaching the lord's deer is punished by the loss of a hand.
Serfs may not leave their village without the reeve's leave.
Every caravan through Greyspire pays one mark in ten.
Since the sickness, the pass is closed by the lord's order.
taboos: Burying the dead without a priest
Speaking a name under both moons

factions.name: House Brannoc
factions.goal: Keep the pass closed and the valley obedient until the heir is found.

factions.name: Millers' Guild
factions.goal: Reopen the pass and profit from grain scarcity.

factions.name: Chapel of the Twin Lights
factions.goal: Turn fear of the sickness into faith and tithes.

factions.name: The Thornwood Band
factions.goal: Feed the poor by robbing the lord's tax wagons.

naming.style: Old-English-like. Given names of two syllables (Aldric, Hilde). Commoners use trade or place surnames (Tanner, of Millford); nobles use house names. Places compound nature words: -ford, -wood, -spire, -mere.

aesthetic.architecture: Half-timbered houses with wattle and daub walls and thatched roofs in villages; grey fieldstone keeps and town walls; wooden market stalls with striped canvas awnings.
aesthetic.clothing: Undyed wool tunics, linen shirts, leather belts and hoods for commoners; dyed blue and green wool for guildfolk; mail and surcoats for soldiers.
aesthetic.music: Lutes, recorders and frame drums; chapel bells.

festivals.name: Twinlight Eve
festivals.description: Both moons full; candles on every sill, confessions at the chapel.

festivals.name: Harvest Home
festivals.description: Feast and market after the grain is in.
